### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A15, A17, A18, A19, A20 and A21 each had several observed successors: about 62% of A15's observed outgoing transitions went to A18 with about 12–14% each to A19, A20 and A21; A18 sent about 53% to A27; A19 sent about 55% to A21 but also about 28% to A17 and 10% to A15; A26 split about 50/50 between A19 and A17. In the later window, each of these activities has essentially one successor: about 99–100% of observed transitions go from A15 to A18, from A17 to A15, from A18 to A19, from A19 to A21, from A21 to A20, from A20 to A27, and from A26 to A17. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- In the later window these transitions form a single fixed chain, A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27: adjacent pairs occur exactly one step apart in about 99–100 in 100 cases (for example A17→A15 in about 995 in 1,000, previously about 56 in 100; A20→A27 in about 995 in 1,000, previously about 47 in 100). [LAG001, LAG006, LAG017, LAG020, LAG022, LAG025]
- Pair orders changed from mixed to fixed. Earlier, A17 and A19 occurred in both orders in equal shares, A15 and A21 about 50/50, and A19 ran before A15 in about 75 in 100 cases; in the later window one order holds in essentially every trace (A15 before A19 in about 995 in 1,000, A18 before A19 in about 995 in 1,000, A17 before A19 in 100 in 100). Both activities of each pair still occur together in every trace in both windows, so participation did not change — only the order did. [REL001, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL008]
- Distances became fixed as well. Earlier, gaps spread over one to five positions (A15 to A20 over one to four steps; A17 to A20 over one to five); in the later window each pair sits at a single gap matching its chain position (A15→A19 always two steps, A15→A21 always three, A15→A27 and A17→A20 always five). Chain-direction pairs also went from being observable in only about a quarter to half of traces to nearly all (A18 before A21 within five steps: 61 of 200 traces earlier, 199 of 200 later). [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG009, LAG010, LAG012, LAG029]
- Relative positions moved consistently with this: A15, A17 and A18 shifted earlier (mean relative position about 0.64→0.59, 0.59→0.56, 0.68→0.62) while A19, A20 and A21 shifted later (about 0.59→0.65, 0.68→0.71, 0.64→0.68). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the ordering constraints among A15, A17, A18, A19, A20 and A21 — entered from A26 and ending at A27 — changed from a mixed, case-dependent order to one fixed sequence, A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27. Earlier, these activities co-occurred in every trace but in varying orders with two to four observed successors each; in the later window each has one observed successor, every pair follows the chain order, and every pair distance matches its position in the chain at ranges of one to five steps. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL001, REL004, REL006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG004, LAG009, LAG029]

This is beyond what an unchanged process typically produces: 50 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.47 expected by chance, each item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, and the items are mutually consistent, since one chain reproduces every successor profile, pair order and pair distance. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR005, REL001, REL006, LAG002, LAG004, LAG009, LAG029]

Limitations: the order and gap indicators use event positions, not clock time, so they establish sequence rather than timing; the earlier mixed order could reflect one flexible process or a mixture of several variants, which the evidence cannot distinguish; and a few reverse-direction gap profiles (for example A19→A18 and A26→A20) rest on a single after-window observation each and were not relied on. [LAG014, LAG015, LAG019, LAG021, LAG028]

Other differences: On a separate part of the process, the elapsed time between consecutive completion events roughly doubled for two pairs into A29: for A22→A29 the mean rose from about 0.9 to about 1.9 hours (98 observations in each window) and for A30→A29 from about 0.2 to about 0.4 hours (102 in each); both rank among the largest differences in 2,000 reference comparisons, and the time family produced 2 items against about 0.006 expected without change. This timing change is a hypothesis in its own right; the evidence provides no link between it and the reordering. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- Two windows: 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 108 units tested, 0.48 items expected without change overall. By family:
  - control_flow: 95 units tested, 50 items, 0.47 expected without change.
  - time: 13 units tested, 2 items, 0.006 expected without change.

So control flow: 50 items vs 0.47 expected — massively many times larger than chance expectation. Time: 2 items vs 0.006 expected — also many times larger (about 333x). Both families have counts many times larger than the chance expectation, so the screening comparison does not lead to "insufficient evidence". 50 items when 0.47 expected is ~106x. 2 items when 0.006 expected is ~333x. So we proceed to judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Evidence items:

Control flow (DIR, POS, REL, LAG):

DIR items (outgoing transition distributions from source activities):
- DIR001 (A15): before: A18 0.62, A21 0.12, A19 0.135, A20 0.125. After: A18 0.995, A21 0.005. So from A15, transitions to A18 became nearly exclusive; transitions to A19, A20, A21 nearly disappeared.
- DIR002 (A17): before: A20 0.055, A19 0.245, A15 0.56, A21 0.14. After: A19 0.005, A15 0.995. From A17, nearly always to A15 afterwards.
- DIR003 (A18): before: A27 0.53, A21 0.185, A19 0.12, A20 0.165. After: A27 0.005, A19 0.995. From A18, nearly always to A19 afterwards.
- DIR004 (A19): before: A21 0.555, A15 0.105, A17 0.275, A18 0.065. After: A15 0.005, A21 0.995. From A19, nearly always to A21 afterwards.
- DIR005 (A20): before: A15 0.195, A18 0.22, A27 0.47, A17 0.115. After: A18 0.005, A27 0.995. From A20, nearly always to A27 afterwards.
- DIR006 (A21): before: A17 0.11, A20 0.655, A15 0.14, A18 0.095. After: A20 1.0. From A21, always to A20 afterwards.
- DIR007 (A26): before: A19 0.5, A17 0.5. After: A17 1.0. From A26, always to A17 afterwards.

So the DIR items show a shift from a mixed/branching structure to a nearly deterministic cycle: A15→A18, A17→A15, A18→A19, A19→A21, A20→A27, A21→A20, A26→A17.

Let me reconstruct: after: A17→A15→A18→A19→A21→A20→A27. And A26→A17. Before, each of these had multiple successors.

Everything is perfectly consistent with a single fixed sequence: A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27.

Before: the DIR profiles show each activity had multiple successors with substantial shares, and REL items show mixed orders (e.g., A15/A19: 25.5% A15 first vs 74.5% A19 first; A17/A19: 50/50; A18/A19: 12% vs 88%). So before, these activities were executed in varying/mixed orders (no fixed order between many pairs), and afterwards they follow one fixed sequence.

So the main hypothesis: the process changed from a flexible/mixed ordering among activities A15, A17, A18, A19, A20, A21 (and A26, A27) to a single fixed sequential order A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27. This is a change in ordering constraints — a change from mixed order to fixed order. Per the instructions: "A change between a fixed order and such a mixed order is a change in ordering constraints, not an exchange of positions."

This is directly supported by REL (ordering shares), DIR (successor concentration), LAG (fixed gaps), and POS (A15/A17/A18 earlier, A19/A20/A21 later — consistent with the new sequence where A15/A17/A18 come before A19/A20/A21... wait, in the new sequence A17→A15→A18→A19→A21→A20. Positions: A17 earliest, then A15, A18, A19, A21, A20. POS shows A15, A17, A18 decreased (earlier) and A19, A20, A21 increased (later). Consistent.)

Note: POS uses event positions, not clock time; a position shift alone doesn't show an activity was moved, but here it's corroborating.

These involve activities A22, A29, A30, which don't appear in the control-flow items. So this is a separate timing change: a hypothesis in its own right (change in timing), doesn't need structural counterpart. Time family: 2 items vs 0.006 expected — many times larger. Both items point the same direction (increased elapsed times into A29). Support 98 and 102 observations in each window — decent.

So the answer: Supported hypothesis for the ordering change? Let's check the criteria.

- Count vs expectation: control flow 50 vs 0.47 — many times larger. Time 2 vs 0.006 — many times larger. So we don't default to insufficient.
- Directness: REL items directly show ordering changes; DIR shows successor concentration; LAG shows fixed gaps. The hypothesis "ordering constraints changed from mixed to a fixed sequence" is directly shown by relational evidence.
- Consistency: all items agree; the reconstructed sequence explains every LAG/DIR/REL item.
- Competing explanations: Could this be a rare-variant sampling artifact? With 200 traces per window and changes of this magnitude (e.g., A15→A18 from 62% to 99.5% of outgoing transitions; A15/A19 order from 25.5/74.5 to 99.5/0.5), and empirical strength 0.995 for all, chance is essentially ruled out by the reference comparisons plus the screening count. Our hypothesis is about ordering constraints (mixed → fixed), which is explicitly described as "a change in ordering constraints, not an exchange of positions." Good.

So the branching collapsed into a single transition. This is consistent with mixed order before → fixed sequence after.

Competing explanations: sampling variation is ruled out by magnitude and screening; the main unresolvable question is what the "mixed" before-order means structurally (e.g., parallelism vs. multiple variants), but the behavioural description stands. I shouldn't over-claim the full chain as "the" process; I can describe it as: in the later window, these activities follow one fixed sequence A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27 (as far as the observed transitions show), whereas before, each of A15, A17, A18, A19, A20, A21 had several successors with sizable shares and many pairs occurred in both orders.

TWAIT002 (A30, A29): from about 0.20 h to 0.40 h — roughly doubled. Both increases, same target activity A29. Counts 98 and 102 in each window. This is a timing change hypothesis in its own right: the elapsed time between consecutive completion events into A29 (from A22 and from A30) roughly doubled. Since A22/A29/A30 don't appear in control-flow items, this is a separate difference — report under "Other differences:".

Per instructions: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:' without adding their activities to the main hypothesis."
